sol.section: 1.5 pw; 16.2–16.4 pointer carriers and ptrtoint/inttoptr rows; 17.4 CC/R lowering; 18.1 C state
sol.problem: Section 1.5 defines pw from address space 0. Section 16.3 then gives "ptr → pw", and section 16.4 maps ptrtoint/inttoptr with "M = pw: v = lift.mov A". These rules do not account for a different representation width in another address space. Witness under target triple x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and datalayout "e-p:64:64-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64": define i64 @f(i64 %x) { %p = inttoptr i64 %x to ptr addrspace(270); %r = ptrtoint ptr addrspace(270) %p to i64; ret i64 %r }. At x=4294967296, LLVM truncates to the 32-bit pointer and zero-extends back, yielding 0. The specified pw=64 map emits two 64-bit moves and yields 4294967296. LLVM 18 and 23 both verify the source and fold its dynamic body to and i64 %x,4294967295; constant source probes fold to ret i64 0 while the prescribed-move equivalent folds to ret i64 4294967296. These probes ran headlessly through stdin/stdout. The dynamic form can survive the supported O0 envelope; it accesses no memory, encounters no UB and is not layout-dependent. The round-4 GEP fix correctly addresses index width, but does not fix this separate representation-width case. [LLVM 18 pointer conversion semantics](https://releases.llvm.org/18.1.8/docs/LangRef.html#inttoptr-to-instruction).
sol.fix: In sections 1.5 and 16.2–16.4 state: "For an integral pointer in address space A, let P(A) be its datalayout representation width, falling back to the datalayout default pointer entry; pw=P(0) is the ISA address width, not the width of every LLVM pointer. inttoptr first truncates or zero-extends its integer operand to P(A); ptrtoint truncates or zero-extends the P(A)-bit pointer value to the destination integer width. Preserve these conversions in constant expressions, parameters, aggregate fields, results and pointer memory operations. GEP computes within its address space's P(A)-bit representation using I(A), preserving only representation bits above I(A). A carrier bridge to ISA addresses must preserve these source semantics; addrspacecast uses the incoming target's conversion semantics rather than an unconditional move." Apply the bridge equally in section 17.4 and the native build, keeping section 18.1 consistent. For the witness, the canonical value computation must be trunc i64 %x to i32 followed by zext i32 to i64 (or an equivalent explicit low-32-bit mask); f(4294967296)=0/code 0 and f(4294967297)=1/code 0. Add a checked dynamic source/map pair and native constant probes. Two viable implementations are (a) normalize nonzero-address-space operations into width-correct integer carriers and target conversion code before the existing map, or (b) carry P(A) explicitly throughout the mapper and bridge at ISA memory operands. I recommend (a), which retains the single-width ISA address model. Do not reject mixed-width layouts; ISA 0.8 integer truncation/extension rows already express this witness.

codex.problem: PT6 defines a load as "the union of AV(X, o′) over the slots o′ that overlap [o, o + size(T))" and also adds whole initializer INT atoms. Union is not byte reconstruction. Witness under datalayout "e-p:64:64": @width = internal constant [2 x i8] [i8 1, i8 1]; in @top, %w = load i16, ptr @width, align 1; %n = zext i16 %w to i64; %h = call ptr @__bennett_qalloc(i64 0, i64 %n); apply gate X twice at index 256 and qfree %h. The concrete load is 257, and the register has 257 wires, so both gates and the clean free succeed. PT6 instead unions the two INT(1) atoms, yielding VS(%w)=VS(%n)={1}; section 3.4 therefore compiles only the width-1 alternative. A compare-tree dispatch cannot handle the actual width 257, or an unconditional width-1 allocation makes the first gate trap T-INDEX. Neither implements the reference execution. I reproduced accept with atoms {INT(1)} and value set {1} in the repository recognizer. LLVM 18 and 23 verify the source, preserve its load through default<O0>, and independently fold it to qalloc(0,257) under instcombine. This contradicts section 5’s explicit claim that the runtime value is always a member of the reference set.
codex.fix: In §5.1–§5.2 state: "Memory atoms carry their storage interval and representation width. A load may copy a whole-value atom only when the load covers that same interval with a compatible representation. A load from a known immutable byte image instead decodes exactly its accessed bytes using DataLayout and the loaded type. For a partial, spanning or overlapping access whose resulting bits are not represented exactly, set the non-handle value to top; do not union component INT values as possible whole loaded values. Any partial store or copy that may affect the loaded interval must participate in this rule. ROOT provenance remains explicit, and §6.2’s partial-handle restrictions remain in force." Make this the fixed reference rule, not an optional precision improvement. For the witness, immutable-image decoding must produce INT(257), finite dispatch {257}, a 257-wire register, two successful X gates at wire 256 and a clean free, with no fault. Add a checked recognition/dispatch execution case and a second case that loads a subrange of a larger stored integer. A fully specified byte-level abstract domain is another valid repair and can retain more finite results for mutable memory; I recommend exact immutable-image decoding plus the stated conservative fallback as the smaller correction.

codex.section: §1.5 pw; §16.3 value widths; §16.4 ptrtoint/inttoptr and pointer rows; §17.4; §18.1
codex.problem: Section 1.5 defines pw as the width of address space 0. Section 16.3 maps pointer values to pw, and section 16.4 says ptrtoint/inttoptr with M=pw is lift.mov. LLVM pointer representation widths can differ by address space, including the x86-64 layout already printed in §18.8. Concrete witness: datalayout "e-p:64:64-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64", triple "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"; define i64 @f(i64 %x) { %p = inttoptr i64 %x to ptr addrspace(270); %r = ptrtoint ptr addrspace(270) %p to i64; ret i64 %r }. At x=4294967296, the first cast truncates to 32 bits and the second zero-extends, so f returns 0. The prescribed pw=64 map performs two moves and returns 4294967296. There is no memory access, poison or fault. LLVM 18 and 23 both verify this function, simplify it to x & 4294967295, and fold its constant-input instance to 0. The round-4 GEP index-width correction is sound for its witness, but does not correct this separate pointer-representation-width error.
codex.fix: In §1.5 introduce P(a), the DataLayout representation width of pointers in address space a, and retain pw=P(0) only for uses that actually concern address space 0. In §16.3–§16.4 state: "A ptr addrspace(a) value has carrier width P(a). inttoptr first truncates or zero-extends its integer operand to P(a); ptrtoint truncates or zero-extends the P(a)-bit representation to its destination integer width. Pointer constants, flattened pointer fields and pointer memory values use P(a), including the corresponding storage size. GEP uses that pointer’s P(a) together with its independently specified index width I(a), preserving only the higher bits of that representation. addrspacecast uses the target’s conversion between the two representations; lift.mov is valid only for a bit-preserving conversion of equal-width representations." Apply the same rules to CC/R and constant expressions. Add the witness with x=4294967296 -> 0 and x=4294967297 -> 1, both code 0; its canonical cast rows are trunc.i32 followed by zext.i64. An alternative is a common wider internal carrier with explicit masking/conversion at every pointer boundary and source-width memory accesses; I recommend per-address-space value widths because they directly follow LLVM types. Do not introduce a nonzero-address-space rejection.

muse.section: SS6.5 (entry-boundary liveness, reference instance bound); SS6.6/PT11 (ROOT(E,i)); SS7.5(b) by reference
muse.problem: BD3-R4-1's new rule is scoped to instances of a qalloc site s whose ROOT(s) reaches persistent memory in the device analysis. Host-mediated accumulation escapes it: a handle supplied as a device-entry parameter (ROOT(E,i), PT11) or returned as a QREG result and passed back by the host breaks the ROOT chain, and SS6.5's bound machinery does not apply to parameter roots at all. Witness (no qalloc site in the module): @stash(ptr %h) stores %h into @slots[%n] and increments @n; @useall() loops j<@n, loads @slots[j], gates X twice, qfrees. Host (REPL, SS6.6) supplies two distinct live registers h1,h2: stash(h1); stash(h2); useall(). I ran the repository recogniser on this module: verdict 'accept', instance_bounds None, blockers [] (same accept with {'make%h': 1} when a @make entry returning its qalloc through an alloca is added). In the reference semantics (SS18.1 persistent state, SS18.3 qalloc/param handles have no per-entry limit, leak check only at program end SS6.6) both registers are live and gate/free cleanly. In the specified ISA-0.8 realisation the @useall load has provenance {ROOT(stash,0)}; SS6.5 dispatches marker operands 'by matching its full tag against current live candidate slots' of an allocation site, and there is no site and no slot variable for a parameter root in @useall's run, and ISA 0.8 has neither qreg.id nor qreg.from_id to recover the register from the tag stored by the earlier @stash entry (SS6.1, BLK-1 (iii)). A plugin following the text must trap T-DEAD on a live handle or invent the BLK-1 mechanism while the verdict says accept; no rule gives this accumulation E=infinity, a fallback size, or the blocked:BD-B-ISA4 verdict, so two conformant implementations compute different results/verdicts on a defined program. The same hole exists for a site whose instance leaves only as a QREG result (alloca-only storage in @make: recogniser gives N(s)=1 accept, yet two host-held instances co-exist and can be stashed as above), because the entry-boundary test requires ROOT(s) in persistent memory in the analysis and the host transfer return->parameter is invisible to PT9/PT11. 'Return' should also cover exits that leave persistent state reusable (materialised early-return after SS14.4 propagation reaches a ret, but a resume/unwind out of an entry in the pre-normalisation CFG is not a ret node).
muse.fix: In SS6.5, immediately after the entry-boundary liveness paragraph, add: 'Parameter and result roots. The same test applies to every candidate root ROOT(E,i) of a handle parameter (SS6.6) and to a qalloc site whose instance may be returned as a device-entry QREG result: if such a root may be live at any exit from a device entry that may receive or return it -- persistent memory (a global, a heap object, or memory reachable from a result or env), or the entry's own QREG result, may hold it, and not every path from its receipt (or from s) through the augmented CFGs, call edges and unwind/resume edges to that exit passes a qfree with provenance exactly that root -- then every marker use of a value whose provenance contains that root and that is loaded from persistent memory is a blocker point of BLK-1 (blocked:BD-B-ISA4), with the bounded static-file fallback and blocker trap of SS25.1, never rejection. The host may supply or retain unboundedly many distinct registers across entry calls (SS6.6), so such a root has no finite instance bound; a handle parameter that is only used directly within the entry that receives it keeps the direct realisation. Under SS7.5(b), substitute reversible-invocation exit and BLK-4 (blocked:BD-B-ISA12) for handles received through env.' Add example=handle-param-cross-entry verdict=blocked:BD-B-ISA4 with the @stash/@useall module above, a blocker line 'BD-B-ISA4 @stash %h: handle parameter may outlive a device-entry return in persistent memory; BLK-1 (ISA-4)', and a state block {"verdict":"blocked:BD-B-ISA4","entry_calls":3,"instances":2,"distinct":true,"live_after":0,"trap":0} executed under the 64-slot fallback with two host-supplied registers. Alternative considered: thread every persistent slot register through plugin-generated launch stubs as hidden QREG arguments/results on every entry; that changes every entry's launch signature and still needs a bound, so the infinity rule (symmetric with the adopted BD3-R4-1 fix) is the right one.

muse.section: SS13.1 (fptosi/fptoui/sitofp/uitofp/lround rows and semantics contract); SS12.7 (N22 expansion list)
muse.problem: The soft-float conversion ABI assumes the integer side fits i128. SS13.1 prescribes sitofp/uitofp from iM as 'sext/zext iM a to i128 (omitted when M=128)' then a call taking i128, and fptosi/fptoui to iM as an i128 call whose result is 'satur[ated] to the bounds of iM, returned sign/zero-extended in i128', then 'trunc i128 to iM'. For M>128 the sext/zext and trunc are invalid IR (wrong direction), the iM saturation bounds do not fit i128, and substituting trunc-to-i128 computes a different function: sitofp of 2^128 (_BitInt(192) value) would give 0.0 instead of 2^128. SS12.7's limb expansions do not include FP conversions, so nothing legalises them and V14 rejects any residual i192 result as BD-E-RESIDUAL. These are ordinary defined programs: clang-18 and clang-23 at -O0 emit 'sitofp i192 %4 to double' and 'fptosi double %4 to i192' from C23 'double to_d(_BitInt(192) x){return (double)x;}' and its inverse (reproduced in this session), and the repository normaliser raises 'N22 unsupported wide operation sitofp' / '... fptosi' on them while SS13's preamble claims 'Every floating-point construct of every format has a row here; none faults' and SS16.1 claims every materialised function is liftable. One conformant plugin rejects (or crashes), another that truncates computes wrong values, a third invents a limb ABI; the text gives none of them the same machine. The same defect covers llvm.fptosi.sat/fptoui.sat and lround/llround/lrint/llrint at M>128.
muse.fix: In SS13.1, after the conversion rows, add: 'Wide integer sides (M>128). Conversions between a floating-point format and iM with M>128 use the limb form of SS12.7: N32 emits, for fptosi/fptoui (and the .sat, lround, llround, lrint, llrint forms), a call void @__bennett_sf_<op>_B_wide(ptr %nz.d.r, C %nz.0.r, i32 M) where %nz.d.r is a shadow-stack slot of L=ceil(M/64) limbs at offsets 8k (SS12.7); the entry point writes the value truncated toward zero (roundings as above), NaN to 0, saturated to the iM bounds, limb 0 least significant, and the limbs are loaded as the instruction's wide result lanes. For sitofp/uitofp from iM with M>128, N32 stores the operand's limbs in such a slot and emits C @__bennett_sf_<op>_B_wide(ptr %nz.s.r, i32 M), correctly rounded from the exact M-bit integer. M<=128 keeps the i128 rows above.' Add normalise/native witness n-fpconv-wide: sitofp i192 limbs [0,0,1] (=2^128) to double = 0x47f0000000000000 carrier bits; fptosi double -1.5 to i192 limbs [0xffffffffffffffff,0xffffffffffffffff,0xffffffffffffffff] (-1 truncated toward zero is -1; use -2.5 -> -2 limbs [0xfffffffffffffffe,all-ones,all-ones] to distinguish), fptosi double 1e300 saturates to 2^191-1 limbs [all-ones,all-ones,0x7fffffffffffffff]; code 0 on clang 18/23 native builds of source and materialised output.

muse.section: SS12.8 (N27 integer intrinsics); SS12.1 (rule order); SS12.4 V14
muse.problem: N27's expansions create or return values of the intrinsic's full width iW after N22 has already run (SS12.1 applies rules in table order, N22 before N27, each to the whole module once), and nothing legalises the results, so any integer intrinsic at W>128 leaves a value that validator V14 rejects with BD-E-RESIDUAL although the program is defined and SS16.1 promises liftability. Witnesses from ordinary front-end output: clang-18/23 emit 'call {i192,i1} @llvm.uadd.with.overflow.i192' from C23 __builtin_add_overflow on unsigned _BitInt(192) (reproduced this session); SS12.8 expands it to add/icmp at i192, and bswap/bitreverse/ctpop/ctlz/cttz/fshl/fshr/sshl.sat/ushl.sat/*.fix/pdep/pext/clmul at i192 to 'call i192 @__bennett_rt_<name>_i192', an i192 call result and parameter. The repository normaliser raises 'N22 unsupported wide operation call' on the uadd.with.overflow.i192 and ctpop.i192 forms. SS12.7's 'a wide parameter or result of an internal device function becomes L limb parameters' cannot save this: the N27-created calls appear after N22, and SS12.7 lists no expansion for the overflow intrinsics' aggregate result or for smax/abs/scmp/sat expansions at wide width. Two plugins diverge in verdict (accept vs reject:BD-E-RESIDUAL) and, for the directly-expanded forms, potentially in overflow flags if the limbs are mishandled.
muse.fix: In SS12.1 add the sentence: 'After N27 and N32, N22 is applied again to every instruction they created whose integer type exceeds 128 bits (only the width legalisation repeats; no other rule re-runs).' In SS12.8 add: 'At W>128 the arithmetic expansions above (smax/smin/umax/umin, abs, scmp/ucmp, the .with.overflow and .sat families) are first emitted at width W and then legalised by the re-applied N22 limb rules of SS12.7 (add/sub with carries/borrows, lexicographic icmp, per-limb select); the overflow bit of uadd.iW is the outgoing carry of the top limb, of usub.iW its outgoing borrow. The runtime-call rows (bswap, bitreverse, ctpop, ctlz, cttz, fshl, fshr, sshl.sat, ushl.sat, smul/umul.fix[.sat], sdiv/udiv.fix[.sat], pdep, pext, clmul) at W>128 instead call void @__bennett_rt_i<W>_<name>(ptr r, ptr a, ptr b) on SS12.7 shadow-stack limb slots, like mul/div, with the same fault rows; ctlz/cttz/ctpop results above 128 are returned in the destination slot in full.' Add witness n-wide-intrinsics: uadd.with.overflow.i192 limbs a=[0xffffffffffffffff,0,0], b=[1,0,0] -> value limbs [0,1,0], overflow 0; a=all-ones x3, b=[1,0,0] -> value [0,0,0], overflow 1; ctpop.i192 of limbs [0xffffffffffffffff,1,0] -> 65; native code 0 on clang 18/23.

muse.problem: N9's expansion covers xchg, the binary operations, min/max/umin/umax (icmp+select) and 'FP ops: their N32 form', but has no form for the atomicrmw operations uinc_wrap and udec_wrap (valid in LLVM 18, 20 and 23; opt-18/opt-23 verify them, reproduced this session) or usub_cond and usub_sat (valid in LLVM 23, verified by opt-23; emitted for conditional/saturating atomic subtraction). The prescribed template '%nz.v.r = <op> T %nz.l.r, v' names no LLVM instruction for these ops, so a plugin following N9 literally leaves an atomicrmw that V6 then rejects (BD-E-RESIDUAL), while a plugin that invents an expansion accepts; BD-E-RESIDUAL's SS22.1 citation (NS SS3.2 validator) does not sanction rejecting a defined atomic construct the dialect promises to sequentialise (SS17.1 single-thread, SS24 D24), and SS16.1 again claims every construct is legalised. Witness: define i32 @f(ptr %p){ %o = atomicrmw uinc_wrap ptr %p, i32 10 seq_cst, align 4 ret i32 %o } in a device function; the repository normaliser raises 'N9 atomicrmw uinc_wrap'. Semantics are LangRef-defined and I confirmed them by native execution on clang-23 (old is returned, the stored value varies): uinc_wrap (10,10)->0, (9,10)->10, (11,10)->0; udec_wrap (0,10)->10, (11,10)->10, (9,10)->8; usub_cond (9,10)->9, (11,10)->1; usub_sat (9,10)->0, (11,10)->1.
muse.fix: In SS12.2 N9 extend the atomicrmw replacement with: '; uinc_wrap: %nz.k.r = icmp uge T %nz.l.r, v, %nz.i.r = add T %nz.l.r, 1, %nz.v.r = select i1 %nz.k.r, T 0, T %nz.i.r; udec_wrap: %nz.k.r = icmp eq T %nz.l.r, 0, %nz.g.r = icmp ugt T %nz.l.r, v, %nz.w.r = or i1 %nz.k.r, %nz.g.r, %nz.d.r = sub T %nz.l.r, 1, %nz.v.r = select i1 %nz.w.r, T v, T %nz.d.r; usub_cond: %nz.k.r = icmp uge T %nz.l.r, v, %nz.s.r = sub T %nz.l.r, v, %nz.v.r = select i1 %nz.k.r, T %nz.s.r, T %nz.l.r; usub_sat: %nz.k.r = icmp uge T %nz.l.r, v, %nz.s.r = sub T %nz.l.r, v, %nz.v.r = select i1 %nz.k.r, T %nz.s.r, T 0 (LangRef atomicrmw; the same single-thread assumption as above)'. Extend n-atomic with native vectors (old,value)->stored: uinc_wrap (9,10)->10, (10,10)->0, (11,10)->0; udec_wrap (0,10)->10, (11,10)->10, (9,10)->8; usub_cond (9,10)->9, (11,10)->1; usub_sat (9,10)->0, (11,10)->1; returned old equals the first component and code=0 (usub pair on LLVM 23, wrap pair on 18/20/23).

muse.section: SS16.4 (getelementptr row, canonical rows for I=pw and I<pw)
muse.problem: The R5 rewrite fixed GEP's arithmetic semantics but dropped the explicit canonical-row algorithm the R4 row stated (per non-constant index: sext/trunc omitted when already at the arithmetic width; const+mul only when element size s!=1; adds in index order with the last row writing v; constant indices and struct offsets accumulated into a single Delta added last, omitted when zero; no dynamic index and Delta=0 gives v=lift.mov P). The new text says only 'Sign-extend/truncate each sequential index to I, multiply by its datalayout allocation size modulo 2^I, and sign-extend/truncate structure offsets to I... Canonical rows for I=pw retain the index-order multiply/add sequence followed by the accumulated constant offset Delta... For I<pw, start with lift.trunc.i<I> P, use the same sequence at width I, then lift.zext... AND P with the pw-bit mask... and OR'. Three readings now diverge in charged rows (SS9.4: one step is one reference row, so they compute different F_B at budgets between the counts, and different reference objects/hashes although SS16 promises byte-identical objects from the text alone): (a) multiply-by-1 for i8 GEPs emitted (const+mul rows) vs omitted; the SS16.6-SS16.10 pinned objects happen to lock this for I=pw but no pinned isa object exists for I<pw (n-gep-index has only normalise/native/state families in Appendix B, and its state lines carry no step counts); (b) struct field offsets as separate cast/add rows vs folded into Delta (the new sentence 'sign-extend/truncate structure offsets to I' reads as a row operation although they are constants); (c) an I<pw GEP with no dynamic index and Delta==0 mod 2^I (e.g. getelementptr i8, ptr %p, i64 4294967296 under e-p:64:64:64:32, the SOL-R4-02 case in constant form) as v=lift.mov P (1 row, the I=pw 'no row' clause) vs trunc+zext+const+and+or (5 rows) vs trunc+const(0)+add+zext+const+and+or (7 rows) -- the repository mapper emits the 5-row form, but the document no longer states it, and this GEP appears in exactly the layout class the R4 fix added. The semantics (values) agree in all readings; the budget fault set and identity do not, which is S0 for the map's stated purpose (SS16, SS9.4, SS7.3 identity).
muse.fix: Replace the SS16.4 GEP row's last two sentences with the explicit algorithm, generalised to I: 'Canonical rows: acc is P (for I<pw, first t = lift.trunc.i<I> P and acc is that temporary). For each non-constant sequential index in order: t = lift.sext.i<I> I (or lift.trunc, omitted when the index is already I wide); if its element allocation size s!=1, c = lift.const.i<I> (s mod 2^I) and t' = lift.mul t c, else t' is t; acc' = lift.add acc t' (a temporary, except as below). Constant sequential indices (sign-extended from their width to I as signed values, scaled by s) and constant struct field offsets accumulate into Delta mod 2^I; after the dynamic sequence, if Delta!=0, c = lift.const.i<I> Delta and acc' = lift.add acc c. For I=pw the last acc' row writes v, and with no dynamic index and Delta=0 the only row is v = lift.mov P. For I<pw the recombination rows are always emitted, in this order, even when the low-I result equals trunc(P): lo = lift.zext.i<pw> acc; c = lift.const.i<pw> <ones above I>; hi = lift.and P c; v = lift.or hi lo.' Add a pinned map witness: lift=gep-index-obj under target datalayout e-p:64:64:64:32 for @f(i64 %i) = ptrtoint(getelementptr i8, inttoptr(4294967296), %i) and the constant form @c() with index 4294967296, with the full isa object= text, hash= lines, and run= lines f(4294967296)=4294967296, f(-1)=8589934591, c()=4294967296 with exact steps= counts from bennett-isa-ref run-oracle, so the I<pw row sequence is locked like SS16.6-SS16.10 lock I=pw.
